content.problemStatement:
Task: The **n-queens** puzzle is the problem of placing `n` queens on an `n x n` chessboard such that no two queens attack each other.

You receive an integer `n`, output *all distinct solutions to the **n-queens puzzle***. You may output the answer in **any order**.

Each solution includes a distinct board configuration of the n-queens' placement, where `'Q'` and `'.'` both indicate a queen and an empty space, respectively.

notes: Solutions may return boards in any order; the judge should compare solution sets rather than relying on a fixed ordering.

code.Python3:
class Solution:
    def solveNQueens(self, n):
        result = []
        pos = [-1] * n
        cols = [False] * n
        diag1 = [False] * (2 * n - 1)
        diag2 = [False] * (2 * n - 1)

        def dfs(row):
            if row == n:
                board = []
                for r in range(n):
                    line = ['.'] * n
                    line[pos[r]] = 'Q'
                    board.append(''.join(line))
                result.append(board)
                return
            for c in range(n):
                a = row + c
                b = row - c + n - 1
                if cols[c] or diag1[a] or diag2[b]:
                    continue
                cols[c] = diag1[a] = diag2[b] = True
                pos[row] = c
                dfs(row + 1)
                cols[c] = diag1[a] = diag2[b] = False

        dfs(0)
        return result

notes: The solver places exactly one queen in each row and rejects any column or diagonal conflict before recursing.
solution.approach: Use backtracking row by row. Track occupied columns and the two diagonal families so an attempted queen placement is accepted only when it cannot attack an existing queen. On reaching row n, construct the board from the recorded queen columns and append it to the result.

better.complexity: Backtracking explores far fewer states than n! in practice; worst-case search remains exponential.
better.description: Build the board one row at a time and prune immediately whenever a column or diagonal is already occupied. This avoids completing invalid partial arrangements.

optimal.complexity: Exponential search time in the worst case, with O(n) auxiliary state excluding the output; each emitted board costs O(n^2) to materialize.
optimal.description: Maintain three constant-time occupancy structures: columns, main diagonals (row + column), and anti-diagonals (row - column). At each row, try every column not present in any structure, recurse, then undo the placement. When all n rows are filled, materialize the board.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n · n!) time in the straightforward permutation-and-check formulation, excluding output storage.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every permutation of queen columns, then test each complete placement for column and diagonal conflicts. This is correct but performs substantial work on invalid partial boards.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n · n!) worst-case search time, plus O(S · n²) to materialize S returned boards.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary recursion and occupancy state, excluding the returned output.
